deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are preparatory notes for Grothendieck's IHES lectures on crystals, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates and Jussila) in Dix exposés, 1968.

Previous page. M^· is a complex of O_X-modules whose differentials are differential operators, on X over S. Its linearization Q^·[M^·] (the cited 'Q^*[M^·]', presumably the analogue of the linearization L(M^·) of Berthelot–Ogus) is a complex of stratified modules. Its cohomology sheaves V^q(M^·) = H^q(Q^·[M^·]) are therefore stratified modules. There is a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p_str(X, V^q(M^·)) ⇒ H^*(X, M^·). Here stratified cohomology is defined by H^p_str(X, V) = H^p(X, C^·_str(V)).

Corollary (end of previous page into this page). Suppose V^q(M^·) = 0 for q ≠ q_0. Then H^n(X, M^·) ≅ H^{n-q_0}_str(X, V^{q_0}(M^·)). So the hypercohomology of a 'differential resolution' depends only on the stratified module V = V^{q_0}(M^·) and on q_0. It does not depend on the particular differential complex chosen to 'resolve' V.

§6 (this page). Let X be smooth over S and V a stratified module on X relative to S. The stratification induces an integrable connection. This gives a canonical de Rham complex Ω^·(V) whose underlying graded module is Ω^·_{X/S} ⊗ V, with differentials that are first-order differential operators.

When S has characteristic zero, one checks that this complex is a differential resolution of V. The canonical map V → Q^·[Ω^·(V)] is a quasi-isomorphism; this is the 'formal Poincaré lemma' noted in the margin. Applying the corollary yields the comparison continued on the next page: H^*_DR(X/S, V) ≅ H^*_str = H^*_cris(X/S, V). This is the infinitesimal/crystalline–de Rham comparison in characteristic 0.

The next page treats arbitrary characteristic. There one only has a canonical filtered map V → Q^·[Ω^·(V)], hence a map H_cris → H_DR. This reflects the failure of the formal Poincaré lemma without divided powers.

Purpose: to explain why de Rham cohomology is intrinsic in characteristic 0 and to motivate crystalline cohomology in characteristic p.
errors: No mathematical errors. The hypotheses (X smooth over S, S of characteristic 0) are exactly the ones needed. In characteristic 0, stratifications are equivalent to integrable connections and the formal Poincaré lemma holds for the linearized de Rham complex.

ideas.what: Hypercohomology of a complex of differential operators depends only on the stratified module it resolves (via the linearization spectral sequence)
